what: Live ordered-lifecycle run of the shipped `tasks` tool in a real Pi-Bolt RPC session (deepseek/deepseek-flash, in-process taskfold attached, stopOnBlock on, criteria required).
how: A scratch project with ACCORDION_HOME seeded (autoArm, defaultConductor taskfold, consent for taskfold-chat-v1) ran one prompt that prescribed nine tool calls in order; the session file supplies the calls and their results.
termination: The probe sent SIGTERM after the single agent_end (exit 143); the session file, not the exit code, is the evidence.

result.text: {"ok":false,"error":"invalid_args","message":"create: leaf 1 \"A\" has 0 acceptance criteria; give 1–3 checkable statements, e.g. tasks add {list: \"live\", tasks: [{title: \"…\", acceptanceCriteria: [\"…\"]}]}."}

{"ok":false,"error":"invalid_transition","message":"Task 2 is not next: leaves start in list order. Call start { list: \"live\", id: \"1\" }. Finish 1 \"A\" first, or block it when it waits on something, or \"move\" this task ahead of it."}

{"ok":false,"error":"invalid_args","message":"A \"delegated\" block needs \"delegate\": the opaque handle of the work you handed elsewhere (agent id, ticket, branch). Its result must come back to this session, which resumes and integrates it before ending."}

{"ok":false,"error":"invalid_transition","message":"The run is stopped: 1 \"A\" waits (delegated to agent-7 — frames render elsewhere). With tasks.stopOnBlock on, a block ends the run: resolve it and resume start { list: \"live\", id: \"1\" }, or block this task too if it waits on the same thing."}

conclusions: A leaf without acceptance criteria is refused with the exact repair call, and create with criteria then succeeds.
Starting the second leaf first is refused with the first leaf's call; starting the first succeeds and delivers its criteria.
A delegated block without a handle is refused, with the handle it succeeds and its label reads 'delegated to agent-7'.
With stopOnBlock on, the later leaf stays refused while the wait is open, and resuming the waiting task is accepted.
The session ends with exactly one doing task; no two leaves run at once.
